 PIRABHAI BHIKHABHAI SENGAL  Versus  STATE OF GUJARAT ==========================================================
Appearance:
MR ASHISH M DAGLI(2203) for the Applicant(s) No. 1 KSHITIJ M AMIN(7572) for the Respondent(s) No. 2 MS DIVYANGNA JHALA, APP for the Respondent(s) No. 1 ==========================================================
 CORAM:HONOURABLE MR. JUSTICE M. R. MENGDEY  Date : 19/10/2023  ORAL ORDER 1.

entities.text: HIGH COURT OF GUJARAT AT AHMEDABAD
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The present application is filed under Section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973, for regular bail in connection with FIR being C.R.NO.11195060230036 of 2023 registered with Vav Police Station, Banaskantha for offence under Sections 306, 376 and 506(2) of the Indian Penal Code.
2. Learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the applicant submits that considering the nature of the offence, the applicant may be enlarged on regular bail by imposing suitable conditions.

He,
therefore, submitted to allow the present application and enlarge the present applicant on bail subject to suitable conditions.

3. Learned advocate appearing for the respondent no.2- original complainant has stated that on 06.01.2023, when the deceased had gone at Aanganwadi , the present applicant had taken disadvantage of her loneliness and had physically abused her and that why after the period of one month from the date of incident, she has suicide.

He has also submitted that since the present applicant had threatened the deceased of dire NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/8778/2023 ORDER DATED: 19/10/2023 undefined consequence, if she informs anybody about the incident, she had Pirabhai Bhikhabhai Sengal vs State Of Gujarat on 19 October, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/90277757/
1 not lodged any FIR as regard the said incident, which has taken place on 06.01.2023.

entities.text: Pirabhai Bhikhabhai Sengal vs State Of Gujarat
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
He, therefore,
submitted to dismiss the present application.
4. Learned APP appearing on behalf of the respondent-State has opposed grant of regular bail looking to the nature and gravity of the offence.

He has submitted that the witness Danabhai whose statement was recorded by the police on 08.02.2023 has categorically stated in his statement that a month prior to the incident, he had heard some cries from the deceased and had therefore gone at Aangawadi where he had found the deceased sitting in the place and the present applicant ran away having seen him.
Thus, the fact of the alleged incident having taken place on 06.01.2023 has been duly stated by the witness-Danabhai in his statement.

Thus, because of the incident on 06.01.2023,
the deceased had committed suicide.
He, therefore, submitted to dismiss the present application.
5. I have heard the learned advocates appearing on behalf of the respective parties and perused the papers.
In present case, the investigation is over and charge-sheet has been filed.

As per the case of prosecution, on 06.01.2023, when the deceased had gone to Aanganwadi, the present applicant had physically abused her and that is why on 07.02.2023, the deceased had committed suicide.
The statement of the husband of the deceased was recorded by the Investigating Officer on 08.02.2023.

In his statement, he has stated that the deceased had informed him about the incident occurred on 06.01.2023 on NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/8778/2023 ORDER DATED: 19/10/2023 undefined that day itself and the deceased wanted to lodged an FIR in that regard, however, since there were chances of humiliation in the society, no FIR was lodged.
It also appears from the record that no suicide note has been found during the course of investigation.
It also appears that there were disputes going on between the family members of the deceased.

6. This Court has also taken into consideration the law laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Sanjay Chandra v. Central Bureau of Investigation, reported in [2012]1 SCC 40.
7.

entities.text: Sanjay Chandra v. Central Bureau of Investigation, reported in [2012]1 SCC 40
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
In the facts and circumstances of the case and considering the nature of the allegations made against the applicant in the FIR, without discussing the evidence in detail, prima facie, this Court is of the opinion that this is a fit case to exercise the discretion and enlarge the applicant on regular bail.
8.
Hence, the present application is allowed.

sentences.text: The authorities will release the applicant only if he is not required in connection with any other offence for the time being.
If breach of any of the above conditions is committed, the Sessions Judge concerned will be free to issue warrant or take appropriate action in the matter.
10. Bail bond to be executed before the lower Court having jurisdiction to try the case.
It will be open for the concerned Court to delete, modify and/or relax any of the above conditions, in accordance with law.
11. At the trial, the trial Court shall not be influenced by the observations of preliminary nature qua the evidence at this stage made by this Court while enlarging the applicant on bail.
12. Rule is made absolute to the aforesaid extent.
Direct service is permitted.
